---
title: "Spada et al. (2011)"
---

> Spada, G., Barletta, V. R., Klemann, V., Riva, R. E. M., Martinec, Z.,
> Gasperini, P., Lund, B., Wolf, D., Vermeersen, L. L. A. and King, M. A.
> (2011). A benchmark study for glacial isostatic adjustment codes.
> *Geophysical Journal International* 185(1), 106-132.
> doi:[10.1111/j.1365-246X.2011.04952.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-246X.2011.04952.x)

Nine codes compared on a spherically symmetric, incompressible, five-layer
earth, with no ocean and no sea level equation. The work was done inside COST
Action ES0701, and Martinec et al. (2018) is its continuation.

The paper divides the work into two classes. Class 1 is the wavenumber
domain: Love numbers, relaxation spectra and the polar motion transfer
function. Class 2 is the spatial domain: surface deformation for an analytic
load. The paper writes a test as "Test X/Y" with Y the class, and the archive
directories are `T01-0X` and `T02-0X`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()))
from IPython.display import Markdown
from gia_mip import cases
rows = ["| Case | Published as | Directory | Title | Contributors |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |"]
for c in cases.cases("spada2011"):
    # The published name links to the test's own page, which shows its inputs.
    page = c["id"].removeprefix("spada2011-")
    rows.append(f"| [`{c['id']}`](../results/index.qmd#{c['id']}) | "
                f"[{c['published_name']}](../cases/spada2011/{page}.py) | "
                f"`{c['reference_data']['directory']}` | "
                f"{c['title']} | {', '.join(c['reference_data']['contributors'])} |")
Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```

Each test has its own page, linked from the second column, which shows the
settings of its case file and its inputs: the loads and the earth model.

Test 6/1 is the only one that uses a different earth model, the 28-layer
VSS96, chosen because the many layers make the root-finding of the normal
mode method hard.

## What we hold

One archive, `spada2011/spada2011-cost-es0701.tar.gz`, holding 977 files: the
contributor data, 87 GMT plotting scripts, Fortran filter programs and the
PostScript figures. It is a working copy repacked with forty-seven operating
system files removed, which the manifest records.

Eleven README files inside the `T02` directories document the VILMA
submissions: `u` is vertical displacement, `v` horizontal, `e` geoid, in
metres and metres per year, with `*cost` the fine grid and `*costg` the
global grid, both poles omitted.

## Reading the data

`scripts/decode_spada_layouts.py` decodes the 87 GMT scripts into
`gia_mip/resources/spada_column_layouts.json`. Its `files` table names every
file a reader uses, keyed by the path under `data/original/`, and says what
each column holds, in which unit and at which epoch, with the evidence. For the
files no script describes, the evidence is the README files, the file headers
and arithmetic on the values: the unit of a spectrum is fixed by comparing it
with the relaxation times of the `.mod` file, and the sign of a residue by the
fluid limit of the normal mode sum at degree 2.

`gia_mip.benchmarks.spada2011` reads those files and writes one NetCDF file per
test to `data/converted/spada2011/`, in the layout of `SpadaResult`. Run
`scripts/convert_spada2011.py` after the decoder. Five tests are converted:

| Test | Converted | Not in the archive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1/1 relaxation spectra | GS, RR, VB, ZM | |
| 2/1 loading Love numbers | GS, RR, VB, ZM | |
| 3/1 tidal Love numbers | GS, RR, VB | ZM |
| 1/2 U, V, N | GS (cap, disc, point), VK (cap, disc) | BL, PG, ZM |
| 2/2 rates of U, V, N | GS (cap, disc, point), VK (cap, disc) | BL, PG |

Tests 4/1, 5/1, 6/1, 7/1 and 3/2 are not converted. Their quantities, the polar
motion transfer function, Love numbers as functions of time, degree-one Love
numbers, polar motion and length of day, are not held by the result class, and
several of their files are not decoded. Each case file records the reason per
contributor in `reference_data.not_converted`.

## Which contributor is the reference

The paper has no reference code: its figures overlay the contributors and it
judges agreement by eye. `gia_mip.benchmarks.metrics.spada_score` therefore
scores a result against each contributor separately, and every row names the
contributor. No average of the contributors is formed, because an average is a
result that no code produced. Where two contributors are available, GS and VK
in tests 1/2 and 2/2, their own difference is the spread a solver can be judged
against: up to 1.7 m in U near the cap edge at 10 kyr, which is 0.6 per cent of
the peak.

## Traps

Every one is an entry in [the corrections](../data/corrections.qmd), pinned to
the versions of the files it was found in. The ones that give a wrong number
with no error:

The `.res` files hold **absolute values** of the residues, because they exist
to make a logarithmic plot. They reconstruct `h`, whose residues have one sign,
and give `l` and `k` wrong. The `.dat` files are signed; read those.

GS's residue lists have **twelve** entries while the relaxation spectrum has
nine. Positions 6, 9 and 12 are Maxwell modes of vanishing strength. Drop them
by fixed position: dropping by magnitude is right at degree 2 and wrong at
degree 128, where a real mode is also small.

VB prints its residues with the **opposite sign** to the other codes, and ZM
lists its modes **fastest first** where the others list them slowest first. The
converted files hold every residue in the paper's convention,
h_f = h_e - sum r_j / s_j, and every mode slowest first.

The `.mod` files of test 1/1 hold the relaxation time tau_j **in years**, not
s_j in 1/kyr: s_j = -1000 / tau_j.

The GS profiles of tests 1/2 and 2/2 put the geoid in **column 5**; column 4 is
the longitudinal displacement, zero along the meridian. The rate files label
column 2 in kyrs, and it is in mm/yr. VK stores rates in m/yr. Beside the six
epoch files, `disp_tinf_cap.dat`, `rate_tinf_cap.dat`, `disp_t3_disc.dat` and
`rate_t3_disc.dat` are runs with a different load mass, and are not converted.
GS's last epoch is a run at 1000 kyr, not the fluid limit, and is stored at 1000.

The point load files in `T02/` are summed to degree 512, where the case
prescribes 128.
